title: Wipeout 2097 graphics by The Designers Republic
lede: The PlayStation anti-gravity racing game whose logos, team brands, and packaging by The Designers Republic defined a techno, club-culture future.
summary: Futuristic racing game with a full brand system of team logos, packaging, and in-game type by The Designers Republic. Psygnosis, 1996.

creator.name: Psygnosis (developer); The Designers Republic (graphics and promotional art)

made: 1996 (PlayStation, Europe, 18 October 1996, per Wikipedia); PC and Saturn ports 1997

evidence.note: Based on Wikipedia and The Designers Republic’s project page. The studio’s page loads its images with scripts and returned no images to a plain fetch. No image of at least 800 px was inspected.

styles.note: A documented source of the look: Wikipedia’s Y2K article names The Designers Republic as sometimes credited with popularizing it, and Wipeout is their best-known work. Its visual traits are not observed here.

context: Wipeout 2097 was developed by Psygnosis; “the promotional art was designed by Sheffield-based The Designers Republic.” The game and its soundtrack “drew heavily on the ‘future UK’ aesthetic of the 1990s—a style defined by techno-inspired visuals and the rise of electronic music and rave culture.” [Wikipedia: Wipeout 2097](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wipeout_2097).
The Designers Republic lists the Wipeout series as a project. [The Designers Republic: Wipeout](https://www.thedesignersrepublic.com/project/wipeout).
Wikipedia says The Designers Republic is sometimes associated with popularizing the Y2K aesthetic. [Wikipedia: Y2K aesthetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y2K_aesthetic).
interpretation: Wipeout gave the late-1990s future a corporate identity: fictional racing teams with logos and sponsor language, treated like real consumer brands. The coded, branded surface of later Y2K graphics follows from this.
It sits at the start of the period, before translucent plastic and chrome web graphics, so it counts as a precursor here.
borrow: Invent a small family of brand marks, each with its own color and code, to populate a futuristic interface.
next: Inspect the packaging and in-game graphics from an archival source (for example the V&A or a museum game collection) and add observed traits.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The game belongs to Sony Interactive Entertainment (Psygnosis); the graphics belong to The Designers Republic.
